All three edge states are in. Let me walk you through the edge situations one at a time.

**Edge A — a brand-new, empty collection.** Open this address: **http://maker:4001/?state=empty** — this shows the app as a first-time user with nothing saved. You should see a calm empty state inviting you to paste your first link, rather than a blank page.

Then come back to the normal page (**http://maker:4001**) for the rest:

**Edge B — an empty view.** Click the **Archived** view (with nothing archived) — it should say there are no archived bookmarks, not look broken. (The **To read** and **Reference** views behave the same way when empty.)

**Edge C — a search that finds nothing.** Type something like **`qwerty`** into search — you should get a clear "nothing matched" message with the collection untouched behind it.

**Edge D — an address that isn't a link.** Type **`not a url`** into the save box and click **Save.** Nothing is saved; instead you get a gentle notice that it doesn't look like a web address, and **what you typed stays put** so you can fix it.

**Edge E — a page whose details can't be loaded.** Some pages can't be reached to fetch a title/preview. I can't force a real network failure inside a prototype, so I've wired a **stand-in trigger**: save **`https://unreachable.example.com/page`**. Instead of failing, the review panel opens in a **fallback** mode — it says the details couldn't be loaded, shows "No preview," and lets you **save it anyway** with a title you type. (If you save without typing one, it falls back to using the address as the title.)

Please try each and tell me if any should behave differently. A couple I'd also like your read on, in words:
- **A very long title or description** — should it wrap and show in full, or be trimmed with the full version still reachable?
- When **page details can't be loaded**, is *save-anyway with a manual title* the right call, versus blocking the save until details load?
